report_name: Malicious Calendar Invite Phishing Campaigns See Explosive Growth

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Threat actors are conducting large-scale phishing campaigns using malicious calendar invitations to bypass security controls and steal corporate credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Link
attack_patterns.description: Attackers send calendar invitations with a malicious link embedded in the event description or location field, directing users to a credential harvesting page.

attack_patterns.name: User Execution: Malicious File
attack_patterns.description: Users are sent emails containing malicious .ics files as attachments. When the user clicks the attachment to add it to their calendar, they are executing the malicious file.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Access Software
attack_patterns.description: In some variations of the attack, victims were led to install the legitimate remote monitoring tool ScreenConnect, which was pre-configured to provide attackers with command-and-control access.

tools.name: ScreenConnect
tools.description: A legitimate remote monitoring and management tool observed being installed on victim machines via malicious Google Calendar invites, pre-configured to give attackers command-and-control access.

campaigns.name: Malicious Calendar Invite Phishing Campaign
campaigns.description: A widespread social engineering campaign leveraging malicious .ics calendar files and invites sent to Microsoft 365 and Google Calendar users. The campaign aims to steal corporate credentials by directing victims to phishing sites, and in some cases, deploy remote access software like ScreenConnect.
campaigns.objective: Corporate credential theft and remote access.

identities.name: Targeted Organizations
identities.description: A class of over 40,000 organizations targeted by a large-scale calendar phishing campaign using .ics files and malicious links.

identities.name: Microsoft 365
identities.description: Microsoft's cloud productivity suite whose calendar features are abused by threat actors to send malicious invitations.

identities.name: Google
identities.description: Provider of Google Calendar, a platform whose features are abused by threat actors to send malicious invitations.

infrastructure.name: Credential Harvesting Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Fake login portals, often disguised as Microsoft login pages, used to capture usernames and passwords from victims who click the links in the malicious calendar events.

indicators.name: Suspicious ICS File Attachment in Email
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious ICS Calendar File Attachment
id: 2b8c0d1e-9f3a-4b6c-8d1e-9f3a4b6c8d1e
status: experimental
description: Detects the presence of .ics calendar file attachments in emails, which are being used in widespread phishing campaigns.
references:
  - https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/10/20/malicious-calendar-invites/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-20
tags:
  - attack.t1566
  - attack.t1204.002
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.ics'
    TargetFilename|contains: '\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\INetCache\Content.Outlook\'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of .ics files in common email client cache locations, which could indicate a user receiving a malicious calendar invite attachment.

indicators.name: ScreenConnect Client Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: ScreenConnect Client Execution
id: 5e8f1a2b-3c4d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d0e1f2a3b
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of the ScreenConnect client, which has been observed being deployed through malicious calendar invites for remote access.
references:
  - https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/10/20/malicious-calendar-invites/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-20
tags:
  - attack.t1219
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\ScreenConnect.Client.exe'
    OriginalFileName: 'ScreenConnect.Client.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of the ScreenConnect remote access tool, which was used by attackers in this campaign for command and control.
